Commentary.Commentary: The chase is underway! Fargana Hoque and Rubya Haider are opening the innings for Bangladesh, while Fatima Sana is set to bowl the first over for Pakistan. Pakistan needs to make a strong start by picking up early wickets. On the other hand, Bangladesh requires a couple of decent partnerships to chase down the target comfortably. The pressure is on, and the intensity is high, let's see how the match unfolds!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Nahida Akter is in for a chat. He praises her bowlers' performance, saying the pitch was conducive to both batting and bowling. She credits sticking to their plans for their success and jokingly says all wickets are her favorite. Akter also expressed confidence in her team's batting ability to chase down targets.

As Bangladesh Women prepare to embark on their run chase, the question lingers in the air - Can they successfully chase down the target, or will the Pakistan Women bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter. Stay tuned as the first delivery of the second inning is not far away.

Following that turn of events, Pakistan Women batters managed to form a few small partnerships, but none could withstand the brilliance of the Bangladesh Women bowlers. Debutant Rabeya Khan made a significant impact with the ball, securing a wicket and delivering two maiden overs. As the innings progressed, the pitch started to show some cracks, which means the deliveries will offer more turns in the second inning which Bangladesh Women batters need to take care off.

Bangladesh Women launched a fierce assault at the beginning of their innings, and the credit goes to the incredible 20-year-old talent, Marufa Akter. Thanks to her exceptional skills, the Bangla Tigress claimed two wickets in the very first over of the match. However, Pakistan Women showed resilience as Muneeba Ali and Rameen Shamim kept their composure, forging a solid partnership of 42 runs. Yet, Nahida Akter swiftly turned the tide by single-handedly dismantling their efforts, taking down both batters in quick succession.

As we wrap up the first inning, Bangladesh Women finds themselves firmly in control. The bowlers delivered an outstanding performance, expertly stifling the opposition's batters. Despite Pakistan Women managing to post 129 runs, their skipper, Fatima Sana, is likely disappointed with the team's batting display. Now, the pressure is on their bowling unit to rise to the challenge to cross the finish line with a smile.

OUT! TAKEN! Shorna Akter finishes the job for the Bangladesh Women! Much fuller, on off, Sadia Iqbal gets down on one knee and looks to slog it but mistimes his stroke. The ball goes in the air towards mid-wicket. Fargana Hoque goes back and takes a fine catch. Pakistan Women are bundled out for a mere 129 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for an exciting contest! Muneeba Ali and Omaima Sohail are ready to open the innings for Pakistan, while Marufa Akter is set to bowl the first over for Bangladesh. The crowd is on the edge of their seats, eager to see how the match unfolds.

The stage is set for the pre-match ceremony! The teams are lined up, and the match officials are in place. The crowd is cheering as the national anthems of Bangladesh and Pakistan are about to be played. First up is the national anthem of Pakistan, followed by the national anthem of Bangladesh. The atmosphere is electric, with fans from both countries showing their team spirit.

According to Russell Arnold's pitch report, the R. Premadasa Stadium is expected to offer favorable batting conditions, with warm and humid weather and a hard pitch with good grass cover that won't slow down or turn much as the game progresses. While recent matches have seen scores over 300, Pakistan might not need to aim that high after electing to bat first. However, dew might become a factor in the evening, potentially impacting the game.

Bangladesh Women's Captain Nigar Sultana expressed satisfaction with batting first, mentioning that they had played a warm-up game at the venue and found it favorable to bat. She highlighted the team's hard work in camps focusing on skills and fitness, which has prepared them well despite limited international matches. Sultana also welcomed Rubya Haider, who is making her international debut.

Pakistan Women's Captain Fatima Sana believes the pitch in Colombo looks good and expects it to be a batting-friendly wicket. She hopes her team can put up a strong performance, acknowledging that every team becomes tough in the World Cup.

Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Fargana Hoque, Rubya Haider, Sharmin Akhter, Nigar Sultana Joty (C)(WK), Sobhana Mostary, Shorna Akter, Fahima Khatun, Nahida Akter, Rabeya Khan, Marufa Akter, Nishita Akter Nishi.
Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Muneeba Ali, Omaima Sohail, Sidra Amin, Aliya Riaz, Natalia Pervaiz, Fatima Sana (C), Sidra Nawaz (WK), Rameen Shamim, Nashra Sandhu, Diana Baig, Sadia Iqbal.
TOSS - Pakistan Women have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.
Will Bangladesh carry their winning momentum forward, or will Pakistan's stars deliver a decisive performance? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Pakistan Women, under the captaincy of Fatima Sana, face a challenge after a warm-up loss to South Africa and a recent 1-2 ODI series defeat against the same opponent. However, they boast serious talent, with the onus on the record-breaking Sidra Ameen and the solid Muneeba Ali to anchor the batting. The middle-order stability from Natalia Pervaiz and Aliya Riaz, combined with a potent spin attack led by Sadia Iqbal and Nashra Sandhu, means Pakistan has all the tools to secure a victory.

Both teams arrive with contrasting form from their warm-up fixtures. Bangladesh Women, led by Nigar Sultana, will be riding high after their thrilling one-run victory over Sri Lanka in the warm-up game. They’ll look to the experienced Sharmin Akhter for runs and debutant Rubya Haider to make an impact, while Marufa Akter spearheads a strong bowling unit featuring the spin of Nahida Akter and Rabeya Khan. That warm-up win should give them a significant morale boost heading into this opening contest.

Get ready for a fascinating all-Asian clash in the Women's ODI World Cup as Bangladesh Women take on Pakistan Women in match number three! The action moves to the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo for what promises to be a tightly contested fixture.
... MATCHDAY ...

The curtain rises on Match Three of the ICC Women’s World Cup 2025 as Bangladesh Women lock horns with Pakistan Women in Colombo. This fixture offers both sides a crucial early opportunity to register a win and build momentum in the tournament. While recent head-to-head encounters may tilt slightly in Bangladesh’s favour, Pakistan's inherent strength and overall balance position them as the more confident outfit heading into this contest. Bangladesh arrive buoyed by their strong performance as runners-up in the recent World Cup Qualifier, demonstrating a capability to compete at this level and suggesting they are well-prepared to carry that form into the main event. Bangladesh's batting effort will be spearheaded by the consistent duo of captain Nigar Sultana and Sharmin Akhter, both of whom amassed over 240 runs during the Qualifier, indicating excellent touch. Their middle order boasts the solidity of Fargana Hoque and the ability to shift gears offered by Ritu Moni. Furthermore, the finishing touches are likely to come from Fahima Khatun, whose late-innings aggression could provide a vital 20-30 run impetus. With the ball, the spin variations of Nahida Akter and Fahima will shoulder the main bowling responsibilities, aiming to stifle the flow and build-up of the opposition. They will be ably supported by the seam of Marufa Akter and the leg-spin threat of Rabeya Khan, both of whom have recent wicket-taking form. Pakistan Women enter the fray following an unbeaten run in the Qualifier, though tempered by a recent 2-1 home series loss to South Africa. The spotlight will undoubtedly be on opener Sidra Amin, who was Pakistan’s leading run-scorer in both the Qualifier and the subsequent home series. Consistency will be key from the likes of Muneeba Ali and Aliya Riaz, with at least one expected to anchor the innings with a substantial contribution of 40-50 runs. The depth provided by Natalia Pervaiz and Sidra Nawaz also offers valuable late-innings hitting potential to maximize the final overs. The strength of the Pakistan attack appears perfectly suited for the typically slow subcontinental tracks. Captain Fatima Sana, who finished as the top wicket-taker in the World Cup Qualifier with 12 scalps, will spearhead the pace battery and look to make early inroads. The spin trio of Nashra Sandhu, Sadia Iqbal, and the experienced Diana Baig possess the variations and control necessary to exploit the conditions, capable of applying pressure and securing crucial breakthroughs to turn the tide of the match. The contest is set to be a tightly-fought affair, primarily hinged on how successfully Bangladesh's in-form batting can negotiate Pakistan’s spin heavy attack.
